newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Thousands of West Bank teachers end strike.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of West Bank teachers end strike.

text.p: Thousands of West Bank teachers returned to work on Wednesday in response to Palestinian Authority warnings to end the first strike by government employees in a self-ruled area, teachers said.

"We are teaching today as a response to an order issued by the Palestinian Authority education directorate that if we don't regulate our work we will lose our jobs," a school principal, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
Palestinian police arrested in the West Bank on Monday more than 25 teachers who were leading a strike in thousands of public schools for higher salaries and improved conditions.
"They (imprisoned teachers) are not against the Palestinian Authority...they are asking for their daily bread," said Jamal Hussam, a teacher in the town of Ramallah.
Approximately 18,000 teachers began a strike at the start of April in the first labour dispute involving Palestinian Authority employees.
About 70 percent of the striking teachers returned to their classes in public schools in the West Bank towns of Hebron, Nablus and Jenin, teachers said.
Teachers have complained they receive about $400 a month, a sum which they say is not enough to cover their basic needs.

Jibril Rajoub, head of the Palestinian Preventive Security in the West Bank, met public school principals in Hebron on Tuesday and they agreed to end the strike, Voice of Palestine Radio said on Wednesday.
Rajoub also met on Wednesday with a teachers committee in Ramallah, where most teachers remained on strike.
"We have partially accepted the demands," Rajoub told reporters after his meeting with the teachers in Ramallah.
Around 500 high school students held a sit-in in front of the education directorate in Nablus demanding that imprisoned teachers be set free.
